implementation_changes.change: Extract the inline provider_config dict from devin_tools into permission_presentation() returning {'permissions': {'deny': list(NATIVE_DENY), 'allow': [f'mcp__foundry__{n}' for n in TOOL_NAMES], 'ask': []}, 'subagents_enabled': False, 'auto_update': False, 'notify': 'never', 'read_config_from': {n: False for n in ['cursor', 'windsurf', 'claude']}}. Add require_permission_presentation(config) that Refuses unless deny contains at least {'read','write','edit','exec','grep','glob','webfetch','fetch','web_search','run_subagent'} and the Read(/**)/Exec(*)/Fetch(*) presentation entries, allow equals exactly the foundry MCP allowlist, ask==[], and subagents_enabled is False. Compatibility: behavior-neutral if current bytes already match; fails closed if deny/allow are weakened or drifted; no auth/autonomy/route changes.
implementation_changes.rationale: Makes CLI permission presentation an explicit, digestable contract distinct from OS bwrap containment, and blocks accidental deny-list weakening before any provider process starts.

implementation_changes.change: Replace inline provider_config with cfg = permission_presentation(); require_permission_presentation(cfg); put(config/'config.json', encoded(cfg)); then re-read the written file and require digest(read_bytes) == digest(encoded(cfg)) before building argv/process_scope. Leave NATIVE_DENY, bwrap client_argv, Broker, socket serve, export size cap, and post-run require(broker/errors/quiescent) unchanged. Compatibility: adds a pre-launch config integrity refuse; does not change successful-path filing or CompletedFailure mapping.
implementation_changes.rationale: Detects presentation/config write faults before an expensive Devin wave while preserving existing transport and cleanup fail-closed gates.

implementation_changes.change: Extract the steps/tool_calls qualification loop from collect_filing into qualify_provider_tool_calls(export) -> list[bytes]. Keep identical Refused reasons: worker step model changed; foreign/native tool attempted (any tool_call lacking server_name=='foundry', or non-mcp_list_tools/mcp_call_tool, or tool_name not in TOOL_NAMES); unexpected discovery scope. collect_filing must call this helper before receipt parity and before parsed_json/validate_filing. Do not classify native/foreign tool failures as CompletedFailure. Compatibility: pure refactor of existing refuse paths; post-qualification filing defects remain CompletedFailure as in the candidate.
implementation_changes.rationale: Gives preflight a deterministic native-exposure detector without duplicating or softening provenance rules; keeps foreign tools and model drift fail-closed at qualification time.

implementation_changes.change: Call qualify_provider_tool_calls(export) first among tool checks; then keep sorted(calls)==sorted(observed) receipt parity; then keep try/except CompletedFailure only around final answer parse/validate_filing/files==[] rewrite. Compatibility: native/read/exec and under-reported export vs broker stay Refused (hold/unknown-capable); only post-qualification filing defects stay CompletedFailure.
implementation_changes.rationale: Preserves the wave08 qualified_filing_fix semantics while ensuring native exposure cannot be salvaged as a mere filing defect.

implementation_changes.change: Add a short framework note stating: (1) bwrap/cgroup is OS containment and does not prove CLI deny enforcement; (2) NATIVE_DENY/allow in config.json is permission presentation only and Devin may still emit native read/exec in export; (3) durable broker receipts plus export qualification are authoritative; (4) large Devin-first waves must run one probe job and refuse wave open on native tools, receipt divergence, broker.uncertain, or non-quiescent cleanup; (5) do not weaken provenance or invoke Codex synthesis to reinterpret unknown/native failures. Compatibility: docs-only; no runtime change.
implementation_changes.rationale: Codifies the OS-vs-CLI distinction operators need so Sol does not mistake sandbox containment for deny enforcement before spending a wave.

preflight_sequence: Confirm working tree changes stay inside tools/construction_swarm and docs/v3/construction-swarm only; abort if any foreign path is staged.
Verify embedded/candidate hashes for foundry_client.py and test_foundry.py match the intended base before editing; refuse to proceed on mismatch (fail-closed provenance).

Run unit tests: test_permission_presentation_is_foundry_only_and_denies_native, test_devin_config_write_binds_permission_digest, test_qualify_provider_tool_calls_refuses_native_read_and_exec, test_export_omitting_broker_receipts_still_refuses_parity, test_malformed_filing_cannot_bypass_execution_qualification (existing), and the new CompletedFailure preservation test.
If LINUX_SCOPE: run LinuxToolsTests isolation/cancel/slot gates; abort wave planning on any non-quiescent or isolation failure.
Launch exactly one cheap Devin probe job on the WSL foundry MCP route with a foundry-only brief that requires list_files then JSON filing; do not open the large worker wave yet.

Qualify the probe via transport exit/quiescent/broker_errors/uncertain gates, require_permission_presentation on the probe config digest, qualify_provider_tool_calls(export), and sorted export calls == broker receipts.

Refuse wave open if the probe export contains native read/exec (or any non-foundry tool), receipt divergence, model drift, cleanup uncertainty, or broker errors; do not salvage via Codex synthesis or provenance weakening.

Only after probe pass, schedule the large Devin-first wave with existing slot caps; keep scientific_execution false and skip any publication/export path that previously showed native tools until re-probe passes.
reservations: Embedded sources are untrusted inputs; Sol must re-hash live files against the stated sha256 values before applying patches—mismatch means needs_evidence, not silent edit.
CLI deny cannot be assumed to prevent native tool emission; the probe still spends one provider call to detect exposure, trading one call to avoid an N-worker wave.
OS bwrap containment limits blast radius of native exec/read but does not make those calls valid evidence; detection remains export/qualification-side.
packet_violation (run_command despite no-run-command brief) is out of scope for this native read/exec presentation fix; do not weaken briefs—track a separate broker allowed_tools deny if needed.
If Devin export remains systematically lossy vs broker receipts, waves stay blocked by design; do not relax sorted(calls)==sorted(observed) to salvage throughput.
No authorization of scientific execution, publication approval, auth/config/autonomy changes, or cleanup uncertainty overrides in this design.
rollout_sequence: Commit 1 (focused): add permission_presentation + require_permission_presentation and wire digest bind in devin_tools; land presentation unit tests. Compatibility: refuse-only additions on drift; successful path unchanged when bytes match.

Commit 2 (focused): extract qualify_provider_tool_calls and call it from collect_filing; land native read/exec and export-omit parity tests; do not alter CompletedFailure mapping. Compatibility: same Refused strings/semantics as candidate qualification.
Commit 3 (focused): add docs/v3/construction-swarm/native-permission-presentation.md describing OS containment vs CLI presentation and the one-probe wave gate.
Operational gate: require probe preflight before any Devin wave sized like wave08; keep unknown/blocked dispositions fail-closed; no config/auth/autonomy edits.
Re-probe after any Devin CLI/binary digest change (existing file_digest(route) check) before resuming large waves to limit wasted provider calls.
design.summary: Treat Devin NATIVE_DENY as CLI permission presentation only; keep fail-closed export/broker qualification for native read/exec and receipt divergence. Extract a testable permission_presentation plus a shared foundry-only tool qualifier, bind config bytes before client launch, and gate large waves on one cheap Devin probe so exposure is detected before N paid workers.

tests.expected: Canonical config passes; each mutation raises Refused. Compatibility: locks presentation contract without requiring a live Devin binary.
